messages:
rohan: Heads-up — PR incoming to the Python client that adds a `route_preference` param and an env toggle. Default behavior won't flip yet, but we want platform feedback before we enable a cost-pref opt-in for customers.

tess: Wait — cost-pref as an opt-in is fine, but what are the observable effects? :thinking_face:

rohan: Main tradeoffs: cheaper model variants + batching => lower unit cost, but p50/p95 latency may increase for latency-sensitive apps. Also the Console's quota attribution currently maps to model family; if variants get used more, dashboards will show split usage.

andrew: We need two things: 1) SDK-level opt-in toggle and explicit header, 2) Console needs to surface "route preference" per route or request sample. Otherwise SRE/support will see weird spikes.

jia: Product wants a conservative rollout: opt-in param + canary at 5% of new installs, not changing default. Also expose the preference in the Routes UI. Can we use a header like `x-rdinfer-route-pref` so Console/routers can tag telemetry?

rohan: Yep. Proposed header example: ```x-rdinfer-route-pref: cost```

tess: We also need a normalized variant tag so the Console can roll up variants to families. Suggest `x-rdinfer-variant: llm-ggml-q4_1` or similar. And a `x-rdinfer-sample` flag for detailed traces.

andrew: Strong +1. Quick note on the internal API: should server-side policy be able to override the header? My vote is header==hint; server policy authoritative. If a tenant forbids lower-tier variants, router ignores the header.

rohan: Agreed — header will be implemented as a preference/hint. If ignored, server responds with a warning header: `x-rdinfer-warning: route-pref-ignored-by-policy`. We'll avoid silently changing customer behavior.

tess: UX request — Console should show a diff preview when toggling preference: predicted cost delta and estimated latency delta using historical traces. Can we add a preview API?

jia: Yes. We'll emit a telemetry event `route_pref_preview` when someone asks for preview, containing route_id, old_pref, new_pref, sample_window. That feeds the Console tile.

andrew: QA items: e2e tests to ensure telemetry events include `route_pref` and `variant` fields. Add regression alert if p50 increases > 15% during canary.

rohan: Rollout plan from SDK side: implement param in v0.4.1 (no default flip), env var `REDWOOD_ROUTE_PREF=cost` for local testing, header injection for opt-in, and a 5% canary signal by flipping opt-in for a small percentage of CI runs. We won't change default until metrics look good.

tess: Migration risk — CI flakes if devs upgrade and unknowingly set env var. Add compatibility tests and clear changelog note. Also add `pref=latency` as explicit fallback param to avoid surprises.

andrew: Implementation detail debate: do we let the client compute `route_pref` or let the router decide based on tenant config? My take: client sends preference, router reconciles with tenant policy and returns final route metadata. Keep decision server-side but surface results to client.

rohan: I'll open the PR with server-side handling as described and include tests that assert the warning header when ignored. Also include example code in README: ```client = RedwoodClient(route_pref='cost')```

ci-bot: deploy job queued: py-client v0.4.1 canary pipeline created (canary_pct=5).

rohan: Thanks — next steps: andrew to add telemetry mappings, tess to own Console tile, jia to draft rollout copy for release notes. I'll link the PR in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
